newsitem.title: UK: German Esso stations consider filing EC complaint.
newsitem.headline: German Esso stations consider filing EC complaint.

text.p: Contract disagreements may prompt some Esso gas stations in Germany to file a complaint with the European Commission against the U.S.-based oil company, a group representing about one-third of the country's total stations said Wednesday.

The Central Association of Petrol and Service Stations, which has a board meeting May 15, may eventually widen its complaint to include Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said Jurgen Ziegner, general secretary of the group.
"The two companies we think are violating European regulations of vertical restraint are Esso and Shell and first we are considering filing a complaint against Esso," he said.

In Germany, the agreement between the oil companies and gas stations, called agency contracts, has given too much power to the oil companies in terminating their relationship at short notice, Ziegner told Reuters.

He also alleged that margins have been cut and rental costs raised in order to compensate for earnings in other Esso markets. German petrol stations are not protected from this under current European regulation, he said.

"What we don't have in Germany is a legal security for rented objects in the commercial sector so the contract can be terminated by both sides within three months to one year and that is the main problem we have," he said.
The group also believes that a businessman running a gas station is not a "real agent" as understood in their agreements, since only a third of their gross margins come from fuel, Ziegner said.
Ziegner said the group speaks for about 5,000 to 6,000 of Germany's 17,500 filling stations, and about 800 of an estimated 1,400 forecourts selling the Esso brand.
Germany's monopoly authority has already been contacted regarding the dispute, he said.
Esso, a unit of oil giant Exxon Corp., said Monday that the EC had requested information from it in response to the complaint.
